rationale: Best-identified study in the realized stratum on the confounding domain and the worst on the domain that matters most for this hypothesis. CONFOUNDING/D.1.a: low — Model 2 adjusts for education, income, employment, all personality traits, AND political attitudes; this is the only realized study that beats the Wall 1 confound by design rather than assertion. COMMON-METHOD: low — the outcome is a register-style birth event from panel records, not a self-report adjacent to the exposure item. REVERSE CAUSALITY: serious — Cox models on worry measured contemporaneously; nothing here separates worry-causes-childlessness from childlessness-causes-worry, and the study does not attempt to. ECOLOGICAL SPECIFICITY: serious, and this is the binding one — after adjusting for the summary score of all other worries, climate change was NOT among the items remaining significant (own health, crime, immigration were). The climate effect is not separable from general worry level, which is the D.3.b/D.3.a boundary failing inside the study. REPORTING: moderate — the abstract's '16 percent' does not match Figure 2's HR 0.86 (14 percent). MEASUREMENT-EXPOSURE: moderate — a single 3-point worry item.

Largest sample in the stratum (N=8027) and a clean null, which makes its risk profile matter less for the direction of the evidence and more for whether the null is credible. It is: adequately powered, sociodemographics controlled, and the authors state the limitation themselves — worries and outcomes are measured at the same time, so results are correlations at the time of survey and not causal predictors. REVERSE CAUSALITY: serious for the same reason, and acknowledged. COMMON-METHOD: moderate — exposure and the attitudinal outcomes share an instrument, though number of children does not. ECOLOGICAL SPECIFICITY: moderate — a general-worries index is included and is itself null, so the study cannot discriminate ecological from general worry, but it also does not claim to.

CONFOUNDING/D.1.a: serious — controls for education, birth year, civil status, income, residence and region, but NOT for political orientation, which is the specific confound that defines this chapter's boundary. REVERSE CAUSALITY: low, and uniquely so — this is the only study in the review that models the reciprocal relationship in both directions over 36 years of panel data. That is what makes it valuable even though its main estimate is null. COMMON-METHOD: low — fertility histories from panel records. REPORTING: moderate — the body narrates 'a roughly 15% lower likelihood of entering fatherhood for men' where Table A3 gives 0.87 (0.72, 1.05), not significant. NOT INDEPENDENT of golovina_2024 (same GSOEP). Working paper with limited review by its own cover page.

MEASUREMENT-EXPOSURE: serious — the exposure is a text-mined index of climate news coverage VOLUME, not any measure of the respondent's own dread; the affective channel enters only through the moderator. CONFOUNDING/D.1.a: serious — the moderator is 'Environmental Attitude [Want to do more]', an environmental aspiration measure, so the reported effect is conditional on the D.1.a construct rather than adjusted for it. REPORTING: serious — no CI or SE is given for any coefficient (stars only), the main effect is null while the abstract leads with the interaction, and the 62% reduction appears to read an interaction coefficient as a subgroup effect. REVERSE CAUSALITY: low — news coverage volume is exogenous to the individual. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

Serious on nearly every domain. SELECTION: serious — 380 students at a single university, a convenience sample with no claim to represent any population. MEASUREMENT: serious on both sides — dichotomous single items for exposure and for intention. COMMON-METHOD: serious — one questionnaire, adjacent items, self-reported throughout, which is the textbook inflation case. CONFOUNDING/D.1.a: serious — no adjustment for political orientation. REVERSE CAUSALITY: serious — cross-sectional. Retained in the chapter for what it is: the only non-Western study in the pool and therefore the only evidence bearing on transportability, not a source of a credible effect size.

CANNOT BE ASSESSED — full text unobtainable as of 2026-07-27 (see the gate decisions file for the four routes tried). Risk of bias must not be graded from an abstract; leaving these fields NR rather than guessing is the honest record. What the abstract establishes is design-level separation of fear from desire and a within-study ecological-vs-general discrimination, which is why the study matters, but neither claim can be risk-assessed until the PDF arrives. This row must be revisited before TICK-053.
